tagline: Around Back Bay, where the wind runs the tides.
intro: From Sandbridge, the southernmost development on Virginia's Atlantic coast, the byway turns inland and works its way around Back Bay on country roads, Indian River and Muddy Creek, Mill Landing and Morris Neck, to Princess Anne Road at Creeds. A second branch follows Princess Anne, Pungo Ferry and Blackwater roads down to the North Carolina line.
The bay itself is a broad, shallow pan of fresh and barely brackish water dotted with marsh islands, the northern end of Currituck Sound. Pungo farmland runs along its western side.

moments.title: Back Bay National Wildlife Refuge
moments.text: Set aside in 1938 for wintering waterfowl, the refuge holds 4.5 miles of dunes and Atlantic beach, reached down Sandpiper Road from Sandbridge.

moments.title: Pungo
moments.text: Pungo's one stoplight, at Princess Anne and Indian River roads, sits south of the city's Green Line, which is there to keep this end of Virginia Beach rural.

moments.title: Mill Landing
moments.text: From this public landing the bay spreads south toward Knotts Island, connected to the ocean only through Oregon Inlet, more than 60 miles away, so the wind and not the moon drives its tides.
